item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Both implement the required Upload method correctly, but B is substantially more mergeable because it stays within scope and verifies uploaded content. A unnecessarily adds an unrelated PersonsService API, directly conflicting with the frozen contract.","reasons":["Both preserve FilesService.Add, reuse multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", propagate helper errors, and route through Add with unchanged options.","B verifies the multipart field, filename, content, and boundary-bearing content type; A never reads or checks the uploaded content.","B limits production changes to the requested FilesService convenience API.","A adds PersonsService.UploadPicture and its tests, violating the instructions to add exactly the specified convenience API and avoid unrelated changes."],"risks_a":["The unrelated public UploadPicture API expands the SDK surface without authorization.","Its multipart test omits content verification.","Neither visible test suite covers empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, or source-reader errors."],"risks_b":["The retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a clearly non-seekable streamed reader.","The retry test does not set RetryAllMethods: true, so it does not directly model the reported POST-retry configuration.","Neither visible test suite covers validation or source-reader errors."]}
